svg.aria-label: ADR-002: training on one reference framework with device agnostic code and one portability rule dictated by the compute plan; serving portable across the runtime matrix; inference runtimes are never training targets
svg.title: ADR-002 — Where portability applies: one rule at training, everything at serving
svg.text: Where portability applies: one precise rule at training, everything at serving
quantum-cortex, original figure for ADR-002. Inference runtimes are never training targets; transparency is about correctness, not wall clock.
Training
One reference framework
the de facto standard is the abstraction layer;
the code is device agnostic, the device a parameter;
the same result across backends up to floating point
non determinism; the configuration hash pins what it can;
a variant framework only if a particular grant materialises
Where a run happens
the paths without an accelerator exist for unit tests
and the CI smoke only, as correctness checks;
pretraining runs on accelerators, full stop:
wall clock is not transparent across backends
The one rule, dictated by the compute plan: the free or granted compute spans three silicons
pure framework ops only; any custom kernel is written in a portable kernel language and is budgeted;
an op tied to one vendor is prohibited, otherwise a granted allocation on other hardware would be unusable;
a kernel proposal arrives with its portable implementation, a fallback pure framework path
and a measured speedup in the ledger that justifies it
benchmark tooling is installed as a dependency where its licence allows, never copied into the repository;
the N1 notebook is written device agnostic, its path without an accelerator exercised only as a correctness smoke test
Serving
Portability is everything: the runtime matrix
the model is served through the inference runtimes of the
runtime matrix and their file formats; that matrix is unchanged;
those runtimes are serving targets only:
never a training target, never an abstraction to train on
The performance clause
the tax of an abstraction layer belongs to the naive or immature ones;
mature layers embed hand tuned kernels, consuming them costs about nothing;
inventing our own compute layer or shipping exotic unbudgeted ops: prohibited
no adoption without performance: the constraint
behind both columns
The question the record answers: should the model be trained on an inference runtime's abstraction layer, hardware agnostic?
Not on an inference runtime: the training abstraction layer already exists and is the reference framework; portability at training reduces to the one rule above, and at serving it is everything.
